draft.title: Has Anyone Seen Smaller LLMs Sacrifice World Knowledge for Coding Skills?
draft.body: An archived Reddit post from May 2025 highlights an intriguing pattern in newer small models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414. According to the author, these models excel at coding and problem solving compared to older counterparts but show noticeably worse world knowledge—even lagging behind some older models with lower benchmark scores. For example, Qwen 3 8B reportedly underperforms older models like Llama 3.1 8B in knowledge, despite better coding skills. The author suspects this trade-off stems from training data focusing more on problem-solving content at the expense of knowledge density. Given these observations, has anyone else noticed a similar split in capabilities? How do you evaluate or prioritize models when you need both strong factual knowledge and problem-solving abilities? Any practical strategies to detect or balance this trade-off would be helpful.
